truth: The Ape King and the Roc are a breath away from civil war over who leads the Court when the tide peaks. The prince the Beast-Butcher Gate killed was the son of the Court's dowager queen, a Void Refinement beast who went into seclusion before the Ape and the Roc were crowned. She has woken, and she remembers.

To become a true dragon the Sovereign needs a dragon pearl from the Age of the Ascent. One sits in a vault on the Floating Peak Continent. The Sovereign is a Body Integration flood dragon; the pearl is his last step to true dragon. Two dragon elders at Void Refinement guard the Palace.
Most beasts of the Age of the Ascent never died. They slept through the Dim Age in the deep mountains, and the tide is waking them one by one.
The next opening is in four years, and both kings mean to fill it with their own clans' young. Whoever wins the most titles will own the next generation of the Court's lords.
The Brindled Lord is old and his core is cracking. The slaughter he is waiting for is meant to feed him enough human blood and qi to mend it.
The page dates from the Severance. One of its three thousand names is an Upper Realm envoy, and Gao Ming has never dared to call that one.
The Gibbon Mother has started editing the dawn songs. Small changes: a decree delayed, a name dropped. She is deciding the war's opening moves before either king does.
The Toad Elder knows what lies under the [[Exhaling Pool]] and that it is waking. He is its descendant.
Under the mud the city is dry, sealed and lit. Its sect left a hall of Ladder-building records that the Tortoise has never let anyone read, not even the [[Armillary Pavilion]].

The Python is waiting for the Fire Rat of the [[Fire Rat Warren]] to wake fully, so he can eat it and break through to Deity Transformation before the war. Then he will choose a side, or replace both kings.

His eldest eaglet was stolen four years ago by a [[Gate of One Heart]] tamer and is now a bonded bird in the Morning Star Continent. He knows the tamer's name, and he is waiting for her to come back for another.

The Matriarch's songs carry under the whole continent. She has heard the [[Scale-Armor Mountain]] breathing for ten years, and she has been teaching the clans an old migration route that leads away from it.

The Kingdom of the Dark Crossing's salt pans sit on a Low-grade yin vein, which is why its carcasses never rot. The vein is swelling with the tide, and the kingdom's children have started to be born cold.

Not all of the ten thousand pillars are stone. A few dozen are Ascent Age beasts that slept so long the karst grew over them, and in the last ten years three have cracked. The oldest of the three is a Body Integration ape, and the White Ape King is its descendant.
One of the nine founding families never fled anything. It was planted by the Jing registry office, and it has sent a list of rooted children to the [[Jing Capital]] every ten years since.
The sages keep a second nest deep under the sand: eggs of the Sea Sovereign's own line, hidden where no one in the sea would think to look.

The council sells the Court's patrol schedules to the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] and the Gang's ivory to the [[Night Banquet Sect]] buyers in the delta. Half the captains do not know what is under their own decks.
The Old Bull has sent his eldest daughter to the White Ape King's court as a guest. If war comes, the herds will stampede through the Roc's supply camps on the first night.
The forest's plants are not separate. Every root in the Sea of Roots is joined to the Root Mother's, and whatever one tree feels, she can feel if she bothers to.

Patriarch Ran Gui has been stuck at late Foundation for forty years and will try for Core Formation this winter on a pill brewed with blood of the waking the [[Thousand-Legs Ridge]] centipede, bought from the [[Jarless Gang]]. If he fails, his three sons will kill each other for the seat.
The queen's lover was a python lord in human form. She has bought a blood-lock talisman from the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] to hide the prince's scales, and the slavers now own the kingdom's future.
The loyalty threads the clan sold to the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]]'s officers have twins, and the twins are not with the Protector-General. They are in a jar in this valley.
Places in the queue are sold by a clerk of Shared Roost City's own council, who also sells the [[Blood-Lock Gang]] a list of who has no one to miss them.
The king cobra of the [[King-Cobra Mere]] has been selling the Golden Python's venom tithe to the Jar-Mothers, the Python's oldest enemies. The Python has noticed.
The Apricot Grove Valley has already bribed a clan daughter to carry out a breeding pair. When the theft is discovered, the Apricot Grove Valley will deny everything and the clan will take the blame.
He spies on the Python for the Roc and on the Roc for the Python. Both kings pay him, and he is saving the money for the day neither of them is king.

Shared Roost City's first lord was the Old Tortoise's half-human son. The Tortoise has never acknowledged him and has never let any beast harm the city; that, not its usefulness, is why it still stands.
The tithe is not tribute. The Tide Mother reports to the Azure Wave Palace on every ship, cargo and passenger that uses the Shared Roost City array harbor.

The Tortoise was the mount of an Ascent Age sect master who climbed the Heaven Ladder and promised to come back down it. He lies beneath the mound, which is the old ferry landing of the [[City Under the Silt]], keeping the place for her.
The Ape King's mother is still alive in the temple's back hall, and she is the only creature he obeys. The Roc knows, and has been thinking about what to do with the knowledge.
Its soul never left. Too old and slow to notice it has no body, it has begun to dream with the tide, and the cutters' nightmares are its dreams.

Some of the cargo he lets through is Court beasts taken alive, young lords' heirs sold for the Night Banquet's tables. Two missing gibbon heralds went this way, and the Gibbon Mother is asking questions.

Sister Hook's buyer is the Night Banquet, but her real employer is Protector-General Yao of the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]], who wants elephant cores to raise Core Formation officers for a throne.
Two of the sealed nests hold no eggs. The Red Helm is hiding a pair of the [[Gate of One Heart]] children there for a debt he owes their mother, and the Roc would kill him for it.
The falcons' Core Formation chief keeps a pet of his own: a human girl he raised from a captive, who reads him the tamers' intercepted letters.
The Grey Plume means to answer neither king. He is negotiating with the [[Protectorate of the Quelled Wilds]] for Jing protection, which would bring imperial soldiers into the bay.
The envoy offered to end the tribute forever if the king tells the Ape where the Tortoise's body really lies. The king's younger brother knows. He was a shell page.

The preserve's first beasts came down the Heaven Ladder as a gift from the Upper Realm. Their bloodlines are Upper Realm bloodlines, and the Beast Court would go to war to keep humans from learning it.

It eats spirit veins. The Storm Roc has been dropping spirit stones down its tunnels for thirty years, hoping a grateful ancient will fight the Ape. Nobody has asked what it will eat when it wakes and the stones run out. The ancient under the plates reached Body Integration in the Age of the Ascent, which is why it eats veins and not stones.
Not all the bones in the deepest gallery belong to dead beasts. Some of the sleepers there are only very thin, and the tide is waking them.
The matriarch reports to both kings. The Roc knows and feeds her lies; the Ape knows the Roc knows, and reads the lies for what they reveal.
Under the glass floor the Roc keeps what he means to burn in his Void Refinement tribulation at the tide's peak: nine thousand years of hoarded lightning-wood. The heir has counted it.
The plant-sense is a seed. Guides swallow one from the forest at their initiation, and after twenty years the oldest stop needing to eat.
The harbor master is a half-blood who reports every arrival to the [[House of Translated Tongues]] in Shared Roost City, which sells the list to the Beast Court.
The Society's best maps come from a gibbon courier of the [[Ridge of Long Calls]] who sells the Court's patrol routes. The Ape King knows, and uses the leak to choose which poachers die.
The fig has a mind. It learned to read in the city's libraries, and it decides which hunters to let out by what they took.
The Forgemaster is forging war gear for the Roc's falcons and the Ape's rhinos at the same time, on her father's orders, and sabotaging one side's order. She has not been told which.
Grandfather Root has a bargain with the [[Rope-Holders' Guild]]: one ginseng child a year, chosen by him, in exchange for the guild keeping other hunters out. He picks the troublemakers.
Qiu Yan wants an Ascent Age beast to puppet, and he has chosen one: the pangolin of the [[Scale-Armor Mountain]]. He does not plan to wait for it to die.
The shard was a nursery for Ascent Age half-bloods. Its last keeper is still inside, and she asks every visitor which of their two bloods they would give up.

Aunt Lan is a half-blood herself and wears her own lock, a looser one that hides her blood but not her cultivation. Breaking it would make her stronger than anyone in the gang, and would show them what she is.
If the Ape King hesitates again, Iron Horn will start the war himself with a raid on the [[High Pastures]], and let the kings argue about it afterward.
The Gate's founder bonded a beast who is now a Nascent Soul lord at court. He has argued the tamers' case for two hundred years without ever saying why.

The withdrawal is a feint aimed at the Storm Roc as much as at the humans. The tigers of the [[Brindled Ridges]] are lying up in the hills, and the Ape King has promised them every human head they take before the rains.
The Drum-Mother wants to be a king. She has been talking to the Storm Roc's envoy, who has promised her the delta when the Tortoise finally dies.
It is a mouth. An Ascent Age toad as large as the marsh lies asleep under the mud, and the High Tide is quickening its breath: once every nine days now, once every eight next year.
The stair led to a ferry that crossed to the central continent. Its moorings still answer a ferry token, though nobody knows what would come to the stair if one were shown.
A tamer and her serpent survived the fall forty years ago, refused the bargain, and still live in a cave halfway down, fed by the bats. The bat lord thinks it is funny.
The eldest Jar-Mother's great Gu came out of this jar as its last survivor. The shard has been breeding a successor ever since, and at the next opening it will be ready.

He is awake. Every ten years an [[Armillary Pavilion]] astronomer comes to the [[Shell Mound]] with one question about how the Heaven Ladder was built, and he answers it, because he wants the Ladder rebuilt more than anyone alive.
Their leader has bred a Gu inside himself from the eggs of the [[Thousand-Legs Ridge]] centipede. It is growing faster than he is.
The Eldest Matriarch has already chosen. She will side with whichever king hands her the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]], every last one of them, alive.
The [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] has found a way in without leaving a scent, using Gu bought from the [[Jarless Gang]]. They took three cores last year, and the herds still do not know.
The Hall's founder achieved full awakening and did go mad. He is chained under the Hall, and the elders draw his blood to make their awakening pills.

Whoever leads the Court when the tide peaks will have the whole vein for a tribulation. That is what the Ape and the Roc are really fighting over: one of them will try for Void Refinement on it, and the vein cannot feed two.
The island quarrel that started the war was staged by a [[Night Banquet Sect]] agent who killed a tiger cub and left a Jing spear in it. The Night Banquet bought the captives afterward.
The King's eldest son is a half-blood, born to a human woman, and has bleached his fur for three hundred years. The Roc's spies are close to finding out.
Last spring the [[Brindled Ridges]] tigers paid the clan to mark every poacher who took a cub's core. The marks wake when the rains come.
The royal line really does descend from Ascent Age ferrymen, and the king's crown is a ferry token of the Heaven Ladder. Nobody alive knows what it opens.
The gardeners are descendants of Severance survivors, cut off for sixty-six thousand years. They are blind, they are kind, and they are running out of seed.
The bat lord rents cells to both kings. The Roc's three captured spies and the Ape's two sit in neighboring cells, and the bat lord has been letting them talk.
The Night Banquet's captains are sounding the coves for a deep harbor. The Banquet Master wants a foothold on Vast Wilds before anyone in Morning Star thinks of it.
The Letter House reads every letter. Any that mention where a herb was found are copied and sold to the [[Rope-Holders' Guild]].
The Apricot Grove Valley elder treats the White Ape King's old wound in secret, and on the Valley Master's orders has been making it slowly worse. The Apricot Grove Valley would like a long war.

The House is the Beast Court's ear in Shared Roost City. Its master reports to the [[Ridge of Long Calls]] gibbons, and its archive of contracts is the best map of human ambition on the Vast Wilds Continent.
It is the last stretch of the road that carried the Root Mother's seed from the foot of the Heaven Ladder to where she now stands. The jade still remembers the weight.

The corpse ships do not come back empty. For twenty years the Storm Roc has been buying the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] puppets through the Kingdom of the Dark Crossing and hiding them in the sea caves: an army that does not need to be fed.

Smoke takes a second toll for herself and lets the [[Tusk-Saw Gang]] pass through her canopy for a share of the ivory. If the Eldest Matriarch learns this, there will be no more leopards on the river.

The eldest Jar-Mother's great Gu ate the Golden Python's elder brother when he led the Court's last march into the valleys, seven hundred years ago. The Python has not forgotten, and he wants a Court strong enough to burn the gorges.
The miasma is alive: one colony of Gu older than the clans. The first Jar-Mother's first jar was a bowl dipped into it.
The Tortoise's question is always the same: is she coming back? The cracks have always said yes.
The Roc's heir has been meeting the Ape King's envoys in secret. He would rather inherit a peaceful Court than his father's war, and he is prepared to arrange for his father not to come home.
Yao has guessed that the Ancestor Emperor is eating the capital's veins. He is not trying to go home. He is building a throne here for the day the [[Jing Capital]] starves.
The Thornwall's roots have reached a Mid-grade vein under the hills and are drinking it. In fifty years the frontier's fields will fail, and the Gate's elders have decided not to mention it.
The grove is not wandering. It is walking away from the [[Exhaling Pool]], because trees feel the ground better than beasts do.
Some of the 'dead' in the Pale City came through from the Nether Shard and were never citizens of Severed Heaven at all.

Some skeletons never stand in Ghost Month: their souls went to the Nether Shard and never came back. Lately the Court has registered returnees under those same names, and nobody has checked the bones.
The shard's sun is not a sun. It is a lamp the Ascent Age left burning, and it is running down: each opening, the day inside is a few breaths shorter.
The founder bought the sect's first lease by selling the Court a list of rebel cultivators. The Court still has the list, in his handwriting.
The townsfolk descend from old Long Dusk people who fled into the shard the day the span fell. Their elders keep a record of that day, including what the Pale Sovereign was doing on the Ladder.

The vales are still sinking, a finger's breadth a year, always toward the span. Something under the Ladder's south face is drawing the land down, and the Sea-Swallowing Mouth grows wider every decade.
The stored light is weaker every year as the dusk deepens. The Sun-Reflecting Gate's engineers have calculated that this Ghost Month or the next, the towers will go dark before midnight.
The founder carried an Upper Realm token fragment out of the deep halls. Doors open for him that open for nobody else, and the Society's best finds come from halls only he can enter.
Yin and yang veins draw each other up. The Shadow-Refining Sect's elders know that a yang vein this close to their own means that, within a century, one will swallow the other.
The guild holds forty years of sun-salt in a vault under Bright Salt Port. It has one buyer for all of it, an agent of the Pale Sovereign offering a price nobody in the guild can explain.
The deacon broke into a hall nobody had opened since the Severance and told the Gate it was empty. It was not, and he is waiting to hear what the thing inside will pay him.
The champion is not empty. Its body's owner never left it, and he has spent two hundred years relearning the world from inside. He is deciding when to stop pretending.
The Tans' register extracts come from a clerk who forges them. Half the bones they sell as moved on belong to souls still living in the Pale City, and two of them have filed complaints.

The temple ferries registered souls too and burns the receipts; two judges in the Pale City take a cut in years. The abbot sends every soul's account to the Thousand Lamps Temple, which is mapping how the registers work.
Most returnees were never Severed Heaven's dead. Something on the far side learned the names in the old registers, and every Ghost Month it sends more.
The grey is spreading north toward the rice coast at about a li a year, and faster since the tide began to rise. The coast kingdoms have noticed their harvests shrinking. Nobody has noticed why.
The Court's notaries keep one year in ten from every transfer. The biggest landlord in the Kingdom of Borrowed Years is the Court.
The Zhi family has been printing extra notes for twenty years and burning them at a hidden shrine. Prices in the ghost markets are rising, and the Court's auditors have started asking why.
The Bureau is not mourning the war. Some of those memories hold the Nameless Sealer's name, and the Sovereign means to own every copy of it.
The dusk is creeping. The flats yield less sun-salt every decade as the Ladder's shadow lengthens with the tide, and in a few centuries the Long Dusk Continent will have no light it can store.

The old king remembers what the old Long Dusk Continent was doing on the Ladder the day it fell, and why the Sovereign forbade anyone to say. He is selling the memory a sliver at a time at the Night Tide Market.
The Marquis was on duty the day the Ladder was cut, and he saw what was climbing it. He has guarded stairs ever since, and he will not let anyone go up.
The sect's Nascent Soul ancestor has not been back in his body for eleven years. The thing that answers for him at sect councils has learned his voice, but not his handwriting.
The foals are not born of living mares. They come through under the Ladder in Ghost Month already grown, and the breeders were told what to say.
The beasts that cross the strait are not hunting. They are fleeing something waking in the mountains of the western Vast Wilds Continent, and every spring there are more of them.
The pass ledger weighs a traveler's remaining lifespan, so the clerks always know who is about to die. They sell the list to the Puppet Gate, whose buyers are waiting at the funeral.
The Gou geomancer's maps are good because her grandmother is still inside the Ladder, as a ghost, and sends them out. The Court would very much like to know how.
The stair-ghosts are not the Long Dusk Continent's dead and are not in any register. They were Upper Realm wardens of the Ladder, and they are still waiting to be relieved.
The pearls are not jade. They form around flakes of an Upper Realm alloy the span sheds, and an Armillary Pavilion agent in Hollow Jade Port buys every one he can find.
The Court can make its own fire now. Its artificers learned to strike cold flame a century ago, and the contract is renewed each year only because the Sovereign has not yet decided to end it.

Ghosts that run short of years fade into the hungry dead. The Court pays its officials in years from the tithe and the passes, and the Sovereign keeps every judge a few decades from empty. Loyalty here is a ration.
The span runs on under the sea for nine thousand li. Divers who reached its end found it smooth as a mirror: cut, not broken. On the Sovereign's orders the Court drowns any diver who says so.

An Upper Realm envoy sealed himself into the highest hall when he saw the Ladder was going to be cut. He is alive, he knows why it was cut, and the Gate's master is three fragments short of a token. Cut off from the Mirror's qi, his cultivation has sunk to Body Integration, and he is still among the strongest on the continent after the Pale Sovereign.
The Xun patriarch has a deal with the Court: when the Court finally moves on the Gate, the Xun will open its back door, and the concessions will be theirs.
The Struck-Off can tell a true Severed Heaven ghost from a Nether-born one by its cold. They keep a list of officials in the Pale City who are the second kind. Nobody believes outlaws.
The fleet did not sink by accident. It was carrying refugees out of Long Dusk the day the Ladder fell, and the sea clans turned it back. The admiral remembers which clans.
The founder's bargain paid the Court with the royal bodies. The Court sold every one of them to the Puppet Gate, and two dead kings now stand guard at the Gate's door.
The Court lets the rebels stand. The Pale Sovereign is quietly testing whether stored light can stop the things that come through under the Ladder in Ghost Month, and her own judges are not told why.
The innkeeper is still there, a climber who refused to go up. He trades with every party and keeps a ledger of who climbed and when. The last entry is dated the day the Ladder was cut.
One memory sold here that year held the Nameless Sealer's name. The Court burned the market to destroy it and missed the jar, which still changes hands, buyer to buyer, unopened.
One shadow is not of anyone killed in the fall. It shows a figure walking away from the span, and it is still moving, a hand's breadth a century, toward the Pale City.
The Gate's master has sold the tower design to a buyer he believes comes from the Evening Sun. The buyer works for the Pale Sovereign.
The old king died thirty years ago. His ghost still wears his body with the Court's leave, and the years given back to the royal family have been feeding it.
The Dim Spring is not a vein. It is a seep from the Nether Shard that runs under the forest from the Ladder's head, and it has grown stronger every year of the tide.

The coast's Year Tithe is counted at the Sand-Watching Mouth before it goes to the Court, and for a century the count has come up a few thousand years short. Someone on the strait is skimming lifespan and selling it to the Myriad Sands Continent.

The Gate can only refine bodies up to Core Formation reliably. Its few Nascent Soul puppets are its war chest, and the Court knows where each one stands, because one of them reports to a judge in the Pale City.
The dean has found register entries in a hand no living clerk writes, enrolling returnees nobody judged. He has told no one. He is afraid he knows whose hand it is.

The Eternal Night Palace has been thawing demons out one at a time to learn how they cultivate. One escaped forty years ago. The host faces south because it came from the north, up the [[Ice Stair]]. Its general would stand at Body Integration in our reckoning.
Traffic on the Ladder ran both ways, and not everything that came down was friendly. Several of today's 'ancient' bloodlines descend from Upper Realm envoys who stayed.
A few masters of the Age of the Ascent survived the whole ebb sealed inside their cave abodes. Some are still asleep.
The Armillary Pavilion is building it. The Seal Watch has quietly doubled its garrison.

The Palace is the one thawing the Frozen Host. The Night Sovereign wants an outer demon's cultivation method. He reached Body Integration and found no road onward. That is why he wants a method from outside the world.

She did not die. The Nameless Sealer reached Tribulation Transcendence inside the seal and is now its keystone. If she ascends or dies, Heaven's Scar opens. It was a two-front war. While the defenders who would become the Seal Watch held the Scar, a second host climbed the [[Ice Stair]] over the north Rim and was frozen on the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]]. The stair is still a door, and nobody guards it.
Apricot Grove Valley sold healing pills to every side and came out the richest sect on the Morning Star Continent.

As the tide ebbed the world drifted off, stretching the Ladder thin. Outer demons, drawn by the breach, climbed it toward the Mirror. The Upper Realm cut the Ladder from its end to save itself, leaving Severed Heaven to the swarm. The ancients spent their lives on the First Sealing of Heaven's Scar.

The Root Mother sprouted from a seed that came down the Heaven Ladder. She is the oldest of the few Mahayana alive in Severed Heaven, and she does not care about anything that walks unless it cuts her.
Parts of the span still answer to Upper Realm tokens.
The floating peaks rise with the tide. In two thousand years the highest will touch the world barrier, and nobody knows what happens then.
The Baili hold the Huyan's debts and carry the Huangfu's freight, and they have promised each clan their best duelist for the challenge. They will deliver to whichever pays more.
Fallen hearts regrow. Several of the Broken Ridges's oldest craters will lift again within a century as the tide rises, carrying whatever has been built on them up into the thin air.
The rods were not built for tribulations. They are a tether staked over the Kui, and each one that falls loosens it.
The Sealed Furnace Peak forges the new Heaven Ladder in segments of star-iron and immortal jade. The finished segments are stored inside the Star Dial's peak, waiting for it to reach the barrier.

The stair was the road from the Floating Peak Continent to the foot of the Heaven Ladder. Its lowest landings still hold waystones that answer to Upper Realm tokens, and the dead of the Kingdom of the Sunken Bell remember how to wake them.
The magistrate was the Sunken Stair's toll-keeper, and he still holds the ledger of everyone who climbed to the Ladder. He is waiting for the waystones to wake.

Peaks are still tearing loose as the tide rises: three new ones in the last century. Within another, most of the Hanging Shade's fields will lie in permanent shade, and the clans' only plan for feeding the ground is to buy the Streams of the Luan's grain.
The Huangfu drained its heart to feed a dying elder and let it drop rather than admit it. The kingdom it crushed had paid them shade rent for nine hundred years.

The slab is a step of the Heaven Ladder, flung here at the Severance. It hums with the [[Ladder Stump]] whenever the Mirror is overhead. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has twice offered to buy it and twice been refused.

The Armillary Pavilion means the Star Dial to be the first peak to touch the world barrier and the new Ladder to rise from it; the Sealed Furnace Peak forges the segments. The Dial's chains are lengthened every year, and the Pavilion pays the Tantai not to ask why.
The blight was seeded by an agent of the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] posing as a herb merchant. He is still in the City of the Rice Measure, selling the cures.

The Crane Burial Temple's founder fled the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] six centuries ago, and his life lamp in the Myriad Sands Continent still burns. He sits alive under the glacier altar, and the Thousand Lamps Temple has finally sent someone to ask why he left.

The Huangfu peak has stopped rising. Its heart is being drained to feed two failing elders, and the clan is borrowing spirit stones from the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] to hold its height until the Huyan challenge is settled.
The garden is the first waystation on the old road to the Ladder. Its manuals are Ascent Age travel permits, and the Armillary Pavilion has been buying every one that comes out.
For three generations the Huyan have poured their own blood into the ground at the Ridge of the Sleeping Kui, hoping the thing beneath will know them when it wakes.
The chief spies on the Baili for the Sea Sovereign and sells what he learns to the Yuwen. He means to be paid by whoever ends up holding the pearl.

Kun blood is half sea. The Sea Sovereign has offered the Baili their herds' safety forever in exchange for help taking the pearl from the Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl, and half the Baili elders want to accept.
The founder was a rootless Huyan whose blood woke at forty, too late to be taken back up. The sect keeps her diary, which describes a voice under the plateau that called her by name.

The high air grows richer in qi every decade, and qi that thick burns the lungs. Within a few centuries the summits and the highest peaks will kill anyone below Nascent Soul. The cranes are only the first to notice.
Half the deeds registered at the Peak-Pawn Market are forgeries. The Geomancers' Guild holds the true ones in its vault, which is why no clan has ever tried to break it.
The shard is a piece of the Ascent Age station that surveyed the Ladder's route. The Armillary Pavilion buys the instruments back because it needs them for the new one.

The plateau folk are right. A thunder ox that reached Body Integration in the Age of the Ascent sleeps under the ridge, and the beating stone is its heart. The Huyan are its keepers by an oath older than their clan name.
Some captives ransomed back from the Palace after last winter's raids hum a tune nobody taught them. The fort commanders have noticed and are quietly drowning them.
The Old Whale is learning to speak. He has begun sending dreams to the village children, and some of them have started singing whale-song in their sleep.

The plateau's thunder is breathing. A Kui of the Ascent Age sleeps under the Ridge of the Sleeping Kui, and as the tide rises its breath grows louder. It is the Huyan's ancestor, and they mean to be standing beside it when it wakes.

The pearl is what holds the Peak of the Torch Dragon's Pearl up. Take it out and the peak falls on the Kingdom of the Falling Shadow within the day, and no Yuwen child will wake again. The Yuwen elders know, and the Sea Sovereign suspects.

The Jing factors are not trading. The Morning Star Continent's heartland harvests are failing, and the dynasty is quietly emptying the Floating Peak Continent's granaries to hide it. The Nangong know, and have already sold next year's crop.
The Society skims a fifth of the shade rent and has spent three centuries buying mooring pillars through ground-born proxies. Whoever holds a pillar can unmoor the peak above it.
The readings are honest but edited. Wenren elders tell the readers which fates to record, so the registers supply the clan with what it needs: soldiers in a lean decade, scholars in a rich one.

The new palace did not surface by chance. It holds a peak heart and is rising like a floating peak; within twenty years it will lift clear of the sea, and whoever holds it then will own a peak no clan granted.
When the famine comes, the Nangong mean to sing the riots down rather than open their granaries, and to blame the hunger on the Jing-loving king of the Kingdom Facing the Dawn.
Three of the nine clans have bought from it. The Zhangsun are one.
Students who take the Armillary Pavilion posts go to the Sealed Furnace Peak and do not come back. The headmaster knows, has told no one, and keeps sending the best.

The Smoke-Keeping Sect's elders have agreed with an Iron Bone chief to leave one pass unwatched the next time the ice bridges. The raiders get a clan-held kingdom to plunder; the Smoke-Keeping Sect gets a disaster to blame on the clans' stinginess.

The Xiezhi line came down the Heaven Ladder with the Upper Realm's judges, one of the three envoy bloodlines. The Sikou still keep the oath of that commission, and only they know what it binds them to do if the Ladder is rebuilt.
Tantai records say the Ascent Age pillars were built to hold the peaks below the world barrier at high tide. The Armillary Pavilion pays the clan a fortune never to tell the Conclave.
The Armillary Pavilion pays the guild to report every find bearing Ladder markings. The guild reports about half of them and sells the rest to the [[Wenren Clan]].

The Baize line came down the Ladder: one of the three envoy bloodlines. The Wenren matriarch has named an outer demon wearing a human face among the Armillary Pavilion's array masters, and is deciding what that is worth.
The core is the elder himself, alive in the mist at Nascent Soul and feeding on whatever wanders in. The Palace harvesters bring him captives.
The drift carries dying peaks southwest, which is why the Broken Ridges is a graveyard. The Geomancers' Guild can tell which peaks are dying a decade before they fall, and it tells the Tantai first.
The torch dragon was an Upper Realm envoy that stayed after the Severance: the Yuwen are the third envoy bloodline, and the pearl was their ancestor's own. It still answers to the Mirror.
Three of the last five Zhangsun children did not wake on their own. The clan bought grafted crane blood from the Blood-Thief Gate and executed the surgeon's family to keep it quiet.
A Armillary Pavilion agent pays the high priest to keep the rumor alive. The Pavilion wants a kingdom of believers ready to haul stone when the time comes.
The rifts follow the Mirror, not the wind. The Armillary Pavilion can predict them to the hour and has never published the tables.

The Ancestor Emperor is dying. The palace array feeds him the capital's veins, and he has decided the dynasty can starve first. He reached Body Integration nine hundred years ago, and a body that strong eats spirit veins the way a mortal eats rice.
Outer demons sometimes climb back up it.
The Sand Sea is spreading. Something buried under it is drinking the oases.
Three channels now flow backward at night, west and down. The guild has bricked them up and told the farmers they ran dry.
The sea clans also bring the Azure Wave Palace's executed here. Three of the skeletons belonged to Nascent Soul sea lords, and their cores were never taken.
That boast is no longer true. The Yu king pledged the river to the water court to rebuild the dikes after the flood of 3,089, and the first rent falls due next year.
The current Pearl King took his beds by seeding a rival's lagoon with a blight bought from a Morning Star herb dealer, and the blight is spreading to his own.

The crater spring has dropped nine zhang in a century. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion has hired every hydromancer it can find under karmic oaths of silence, and is quietly buying the third of the oases' water rights that Thousand Lamps Temple does not already hold.
The khan's spear method came from an outcast of the [[Valley of Snuffed Lamps]], who wants a horde that will ride up the Roof road one day, and is patient.
The Shi family's eldest daughter was sent north as a hostage to the [[Eternal Night Palace]] twenty years ago. She came home last winter as an inner disciple, and she has not aged a day.
The noon wind is not weather. An Ascent Age array at the valley head still pulls the gang wind down once a day to guard something under the deepest ice.
The garden belonged to the lord under the [[Thirsting Sands]]. Its herbs are the only medicine that can wake him early, or keep him asleep.
The highest landing anyone has reached has a door in it. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion sells the tokens partly to find out who can open it.
The magistrate wants to live again and is bargaining with the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] for an immortal's body to wear. The Court of No Light does not know.
The Worm Mother is fleeing, not hunting. Her brood has moved twenty li east every year since she woke, away from the [[Thirsting Sands]].
The founder walked into a rift near the [[Ladder Stump]] and walked out a century later, unaged. The sect keeps her in its deepest hall, and she has never said where she was.
The fog is thinning. Fifty years ago it came every morning; now it misses one morning in five, and the Net Mothers have begun rationing without saying why.
The volume of the falls has dropped by a fifth in a hundred years. The snowfall on the Roof has not.
Two of the temple's senior monks are the Thousand Lamps Temple monks whose lamps still burn in the great hall. The temple is the arm the Thousand Lamps Temple cannot be seen to have.
The king died nine years ago. His chief alchemist wears the mask and has been trading the kingdom's best veins to the [[Blood Sand Gate]] for protection.
The Lamplighters' Guild is run by an outcast from the Valley of Snuffed Lamps. The Thousand Lamps Temple knows and allows it, because a criminal it understands is better than one it doesn't.
The abbey does not know where it sends the souls. Its founder's rite opens a road toward the [[Nether Shard]], not toward rebirth.
Some of the oldest caves open into Ascent Age halls inside the Wall. The Cliff Lord sells the way in, one hall at a time, to the [[House of City-Openers]] diggers.
The khan has a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] banker in his tent. The Pavilion is financing his war on credit, against the oasis water rights he means to take.
The Hall is a landlord, not a court. Two thirds of the oases' water deeds lie in its vault under the Thousand Lamps Temple's seal, and its allotments follow the rents.
The glaciers are not melting from the tide's warmth. Their meltwater is being pulled down through the rock toward the thing buried under the Sand Sea, and the ice is thinning from below.
A starving Ma king signed the springs over to the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] four thousand years ago in exchange for famine grain. The family has no idea it rents its own water.
Not every body in the columns was dead when it was bought. The elders have a binding talisman that works on the living, and it is their best seller.
The cistern refills itself from somewhere below floor four hundred. The Sun family has never told anyone, because the price of water is how they rule.
A quicksilver spirit lives in the deepest pool and has been drinking alchemists for a thousand years. It is why the vapor brings visions instead of simply killing.
Every reading is sold twice: once to the person who asked, and once to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]]'s information desk.
The chieftess is negotiating a marriage alliance with the king of the Kingdom of Yellow Wheat, and has told her tribe the opposite.
Some of the floating shards in the mirages over the water are not mirages. One has drifted closer to the coast every year for a decade, and the port families are already arguing over who owns it.
The matriarch pays the Heavenly Scale Pavilion for news of the Sea Sovereign. She means to be on the winning side when the Sovereign tries to become a true dragon.
The Red Wind is old and failing, and two young stallions are waiting. A tamer who backed the right one could own the herd.
Two clan heads have sold their own grandparents' bodies to corpse buyers and blamed lowland thieves. The vulture monks suspect one of them.
The lake has dropped a hand's width a year for a century. Duo engineers found a crack in the lakebed that hums, and the family sealed it with a formation and told nobody.
The king has promised his daughter to both the khan and the Gyrfalcon chieftess, and hopes one of them kills the other first.
The Great Escort House sells one caravan route in fifty to the Thirsting Heart Sect, and its own caravans are never touched.
The Heavenly Scale Pavilion's water desk knows to the season when the Kingdom of the Desert Poplars's last wells will fail. The loan falls due eight months later.
The Khan's body is not here, but his clan's ancestor stone is, under the largest cairn. The tribes in the Black Frost Continent would give almost anything to get it back.

The ice forms early because the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]] is advancing south. The Lion's Roar Cloister's abbot has known for thirty years and has written to the [[Seal Watch]] eleven times without an answer.
The master is the khan's mother. She left the tribe when he was two, and neither of them has told anyone.
None of the three boys is the reborn prince. The real one is a girl in a Black Yak herding camp. The regent recognized her at a sky burial last year and has been paying her family to keep moving.
The nuns have treated three [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders whose wounds closed overnight and whose blood was the wrong color. They burned the bandages and told only the abbess.
The abbot's ledger of released bodies has false lines. The order sells one cultivator body in ten to the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] and uses the money to buy the rest back from thieves.
The House of City-Openers is a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] subsidiary in all but name. The Pavilion owns six tenths of it through three shell houses and sees every find before it is appraised.

Under the center sleeps the lord of the river cities, an Ascent Age cultivator who sealed himself away as the Ebb began. His preservation array has been drinking the land ever since, and as the tide wakes him it drinks faster. He sealed himself at Body Integration.
Their prayers are answered. The thing under the sand gives back a little of what it drinks to those who feed it, and the sect master has heard it speak.
Its illusions fail wherever the new mirages appear. Something else is painting pictures on the pan, and the sect master has forbidden his disciples to look at them.
Half the Ascent Age relics sold at the Grand Auction pass through the Withered Rivers on their way west, and a third of all of them were made here.
The numbers are dates: the years the seal weakened most. All but the last have already happened, and the last is less than ten years away.
The king pays the [[Eternal Night Palace]] a yearly tribute of twenty mortals to spare his own fort. The villages chosen believe raiders took them.
The guild has quietly stopped routing caravans through four western oases. It knows their wells will fail within a decade, and would rather they die without its trade than with it.
The vein is not new. An Ascent Age array sealed it under the ice, and the array is still running further up the slope, beneath ice that has not melted yet.
Every geomancer who has mapped the water table here has found the same thing: it slopes toward the [[Thirsting Sands]] from every direction, uphill included.
The valley's eldest outcast was expelled for asking what the monk in the deepest hall is meditating on. He has a Nascent Soul and an answer.
The stele is real. It was cut by the last cultivator who tried to fly from the summit to the Mirror after the Ladder broke, and his body is still sitting beside it.
The Ferry King drowned four years ago. His ghost still rules, because the guild masters found him more reasonable afterward.
The dew arrays yield less every year. The air over the Sand Sea is drying faster than the elders can explain, and they have stopped publishing their measurements.
She is the only glacier in Myriad Sands that is still growing. Whatever is pulling water from under the Roof's other glaciers has not reached her yet.
The spirit poplars are walking west, toward the [[Thirsting Sands]], following the water down. A grove that reaches the edge drinks itself to death in a season.
The Heavenly Scale Pavilion lent the Lu family the money to build the pans, and lent the Ban family the money to fight them. Whoever wins, the Pavilion owns the salt.
The oldest bull carries an Ascent Age harpoon in its back, stamped with the seal of the river cities. It slept through the Dim Age with the harpoon in it.
The black ice is not ice. It is the frozen blood of an outer demon killed at the Severance, and the worms that eat it are changing.
The mirages have grown sharper every year since the tide began rising, and some now show places that are not in Severed Heaven at all. Even the sect that hunts with them is afraid of those.
Each year the river ends a few li further upstream. The last white flood was sixty years ago, and the bed has not run since.
Forty captured blood cultivators live in the lower cells. Six have truly repented. Two are spying for the Night Sovereign; the abbot knows which two and feeds them lies.
They do face west on the longest night. The array is a ward against something in the Buried Cities, and the broken places are where tribes took stones for their hearths.

The archive can unmake an oath as well as witness it. The Hall has done it twice, both times at the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]]'s request, and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion has never learned which of its contracts failed.
The grave militia sells the bodies of the thieves it kills to the same buyers, and paid for the kingdom's new walls that way.
The river is not failing at the top. The Roof sends down as much water as ever; the delta is losing it into the ground, and the lost water slopes west toward the [[Thirsting Sands]].
Some splinters still answer Upper Realm tokens, as the Fallen Ladder does. The Workshop sells those to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] alone, at ten times the price, and asks no questions.
Some rekeyed guardians still obey their first masters underneath. Three of the Workshop's puppets left their posts in the same month this year, all walking west.
The oldest dune-songs describe the cities before the sand: green, rich, and singing about a lord under the river who must not be woken.

The star families' records show the Stump's hum growing louder every decade. They have sold copies to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] and to a polite buyer who hums while he reads, and they did not recognize the [[Void Choir]] in him.
One of the Net Mothers is a shark-folk half-blood. She is the reason the Cold Tide Clan has never raided the Kingdom of Fog Nets, and the other Mothers know exactly what she is.
One lamp in the deepest hall has not flickered in nine thousand years. Its monk is why the Askers always find their answer: he hears every lie told within sight of the Wall.
Most of what Kingdom of Mended Antiquities sells was never broken, because it never existed. The guild forges Ascent Age relics from scratch, and its work has sold at three Grand Auctions.
The Blood Sand Gate's master is the younger brother of the Temple of the Merciful Blade's abbot. They meet each year at the Dead Falls to agree how many of each other's people to kill.
The pact's full text, kept in the Cloister, gives the lions one human child every hundred years. The monks have paid it eight times and told no one.
The Bridge Elders pay the [[Blood Sand Gate]] a tenth of every toll, and in return the sect robs every caravan that tries the fords instead.
The Ban family has hired the Gate of the Empty City to lure sea-salt caravans into the pan. Three have vanished this year.
Its founder left because he found that a third of the Grand Auction's Ascent Age relics were made in the Withered Rivers. The Pavilion of True Assay still has his notes and has never published them.
Last spring the lamps brought in a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] ship. The Gou family has its cargo and three of its crew in the cellars, and has not decided which is more dangerous to keep.

The [[Court of No Light]] counts the Myriad Sands Continent's dead from its registry office in the City of Evening Light as carefully as its own, and is preparing a legal claim on every soul that dies within sight of the strait.
The overflow has fallen by a third in a century. Fallen Star City's council has already voted, in secret, to close the tunnel when it falls by half.
The ship came down the Heaven Ladder, not up it. The log sealed in the captain's cabin names who was aboard, and some of those names are carried today by families in the Floating Peak Continent.
Some of the Kingdom of Counting Houses's debts were bought, not lent. A Guild bureau buys bad debts on six continents and brings the debtors here through the Fallen Star City array.
The wind sect sealed its techniques in the frost cranes. Kill a crane and its method is lost; tame one and, in time, it teaches.
The tithe rose because nine hundred new lamps were lit last year, more than in any year since the Outer Demon War. The temple is recruiting, and it has not said what for.

The Bone Ancestor sleeping inside Ancestor Mountain is a Deity Transformation body cultivator from the Dim Age, and he is waking up. Two war chiefs have quietly reached Deity Transformation in body. The tribes only count the Ancestor.

Half the League's pirate lords pay tribute to the Azure Wave Palace for safe passage. The other half don't know. Three of the League's island masters are at Deity Transformation, and each believes the other two are not.

The eldest Jar-Mother keeps a Gu that has eaten a Nascent Soul. It is the real reason the Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains leaves the valleys alone. She reached Deity Transformation forty years ago and lets the clans believe she is still Nascent Soul.
The Mirror's immortals cut the Heaven Ladder from their end. They have not forgotten Severed Heaven, and they are watching the tide too.
Under the Fallen Ladder the barrier to the Nether Shard never fully closes. Things come through that were never alive in Severed Heaven.
The Banquet Master reached Deity Transformation sixty years ago and is hiding it, waiting for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's ancestor to die.

Three of the nine bloodlines come from Upper Realm envoys who stayed after the Severance. The Conclave's Old Ancestor is a Mahayana who still remembers the Mirror's language. Below him, the First Elder is at Body Integration and three clan ancestors are at Void Refinement.

The Sealer's name was erased from the living, not the dead. The Pale Sovereign remembers it and keeps it as leverage. Under her, the Chief Judge is a Body Integration ghost and two judges sit at Void Refinement.

The Thousand Lamps Temple owns the water rights to two thirds of the Myriad Sands Continent's oases, and its compassion has a price list. A monk in the deepest hall has been meditating for nine thousand years and reached Mahayana without telling anyone. The Abbot is at Body Integration and believes he is the temple's peak.
The three spirit veins under Jing Capital are being drained to keep the Ancestor Emperor alive, and the heartland's harvests are failing because of it.
The founding ancestor, a Void Refinement sword cultivator, is still in seclusion under the main peak. He stopped answering summons two hundred years ago, and the elders are afraid to look.
Lady Gongsun Wei, the general's widow, has been trading cores and captives to Shared Roost City to buy the weapons the capital stopped sending.
The wreck's hold is sealed and still warm.
The Beast Court is not sending the raids. Old beasts are waking in the Vast Wilds Continent's mountains and driving the young ones north across the strait.
The prince's 'grain shortfall' is stockpiled in a hollowed mountain under his horse farms, enough to feed an army of millions for two years.
The fleet's commander is Prince Rui's man. If the succession comes to war, the southern fleet will decide who controls the sea road to the frontier.
The new vein is not natural. It is the core of an Ascent Age fire array waking with the tide, and the whole range is its wall.
The Cinnabar Hill Sect's master is buying blight samples from the Netherworm Stockade to make a blight of his own.
Anyone who compares the logs will see the mist has fallen by half in three centuries, starting the year the Ancestor Emperor withdrew.
The Dawn League has been offered help by the Night Banquet. The price is the passes, and the League's elder council is about to say yes.
The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has quietly doubled its recruiting since its founder fell silent. The sect masters want more swords before anyone tests them.
The tide tables have stopped matching the sea. As the Mirror swells, its pull lifts the outer ocean a little higher every year, and the pavilion's tables were built for a world that is gone.
The thinning spreads south from the Jing Capital along the old vein courses. The Granary's soil is fine; the qi under it is being pulled north.
The tree can feel the drain flowing toward the palace and could lead anyone to the array's outer nodes. It has not found anyone it trusts.
The guild pays the Azure Wave Palace with information about the coast, not silk.
The glacier the Cold Forge depends on is melting as the tide rises. The clan has twenty years of ice left and has told nobody.
The dead fields form rings around the Jing Capital that match the palace array's draw. Court astrologers who noticed were posted to the frontier; two never arrived.
The sect's founder found this realm, ate at its table for nine nights and came out with the Banquet's devouring method.
Half of the Gate of Fine Grain's failure really is the Apricot Grove Valley blight, planted ten years ago. The other half is the drain. The elders cannot tell the two apart, and that is the problem.
The main peak's sword hum, which every disciple hears in meditation, faded two hundred years ago. The elders replaced it with an array that imitates it.
Some graves are empty. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect buries the swords of disciples it executed in secret beside the honored dead.
The commander has received orders under the Ancestor Emperor's seal for forty years. Lately the brushwork has changed.
The nine points form a fragment of an Ascent Age tribulation array. Someone could finish it.
The locusts are hatching from soil emptied of qi. Wherever the drain runs deepest, they appear first.
The logs show the Stump's hum rising with the tide, faster each decade. The abbot sent the figures to the Armillary Pavilion and has been paid every year since to stop publishing them.
Fang Ru was sent down from the inner sect for a crime the sect never names. He has been writing to the Night Banquet.
Beast Court envoys have offered the king a seat at the Court's lowest table if his packs drive the loggers out of the groves for good. He has not decided.
The Jiao patriarch has bought one of the Gate's immortal-corpse puppets in secret to study it. It watches him when he works.
The storms have doubled in ten years. Something far out toward the Rim is drawing them, and the lightning sect's elders have felt it calling.
One rift in ten opens toward the Scar. What comes through those does not wash back out.
Since the harvests failed the Registry has been ordered to send every root above middling straight to the palace, unrecorded. None of those children have been assigned anywhere.
The ones who come back are not all the ones who left. A few are Banquet disciples wearing their faces, and they go on to serve in noble houses across the Morning Star Continent.
The Banner's leader hums a tune nobody taught him, and his followers have started humming it too.
Straw golems that are smashed reform in the shape of whoever smashed them.
Prince Rui's agents have been buying the best foals through false sales. The Stables' master knows and has been paid to know.
Three of their strains were stolen from a Jar-Mother village. The thief is the Stockade's master, and the Jar-Mothers already know.
The marsh grows wherever the Banquet Master's aura settles. That cultivation has outgrown Nascent Soul, and the land is the first thing that cannot hide it.

The kingdom's best stallion bloodline comes from a beast that wandered over the strait on its own and asked to stay. It speaks, though it has never shown a realm that should allow it, and has asked them to keep that quiet.
The vein feeding the lower steps has started running backward, downhill toward the Jing Capital.
The last crew back brought up a jade token that hums in time with the Stump. The Society's master has hidden it and is selling dive rights to the spot.
The king's eldest daughter tested as a heaven-grade root. He hid it, and now both sides know.
The Li patriarch's grandson was conscripted by the Registry eight years ago and has not been heard from. The patriarch blames the throne.
One in ten children never reaches the Stair. They go south down the river to the marsh buyers, and the Gang tells the families they failed the climb.
King Dou sells captured pirates to the Convict Prefecture as miners instead of hanging them. Three of his recent captures were pirate lords' sons, sent to recruit in the pits.
The abbot has read the drain in the earth and knows who causes it. He keeps silent because the court has promised the temple a hundred thousand acres when the famine ends.
The mausoleum's guardian array runs off the same veins as the palace. Since the drain began, the spear-spirits have been starving, and they have started to wander off the hill.
The ghosts on the battlefield have started marching in formation toward the coast every Ghost Month, as if called to a wall.
King Hao's court geomancer has found that the soil's qi runs north like water down a drain, and is too frightened to tell him why.
The Bais bribe the Registry with one rooted child in three to keep the other two. They do not choose randomly.
Old Ma has been luring the Azure Wave Palace's own toll ships onto the reefs, and blaming the storms.
The stele's carver was an Ascent Age master who walked out along the falling water, as the old texts claim, and came back. The worn last line tells how.
The Coin Treasure Trading House insures grain ships, then sells their routes to pirates. It profits twice and has done so for forty years.
The cave-in was deliberate. The buried shaft broke into an Ascent Age gallery, and the Kangs wanted no witnesses.
The sect's Nascent Soul master killed a young Beast Court prince fifty years ago. The prince's mother has finally woken from seclusion.
Those who sit on the beach long enough start to hear the hum as a song. Some fishing villages have been singing along for a year.
One exile is not bloodless: his bloodline was sealed at birth by a rival clan. The Conclave has learned of it and wants him back, quietly.
The warden has been writing off living convicts as dead and selling them south to the marsh buyers.
The Society's doctors have mapped the blight's spread across three regions. Their map points back to the valley.
The blight the Apricot Grove Valley seeds in rival gardens has started jumping to its own tenants' fields, and the valley's healers cannot cure what their elders made.
The house master is the Night Bridge’s fifth Core Formation leader, the one the Society counts as dead.
The master can hear a voice in the storms from the east. He believes it is his Dao calling him to the Rim.
The river's qi drops sharply as it passes the Jing Capital and recovers a hundred li downstream. Fishermen have noticed; officials have not written it down.
The vein under the Imperial Grain Prefecture is a capillary of the Jing Capital veins. It is not failing. It is being pulled.
The manuals are a Dim Age Wind Dao method, complete through Core Formation.
The sect's banners can no longer turn the dead. They are being pulled toward the coast by something stronger, and the sect is pretending it planned the marches.
The Apricot Grove Valley's blight was carried into the caves by a gardener the valley bought. He still works for the king.
The Vermilion Talisman Sect's cinnabar seam runs into the root of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's main peak. The miners have started hearing a sword hum in the rock, very faintly.
A jiao of the Azure Wave Palace's court nests its young in a sea cave off this coast. If one is ever taken, the sea clans will come ashore.
The villagers have started humming a tune nobody taught them, all at the same hour of the night.
They are not gone. A few slipped out during the war and wear human faces. The Void Choir hears the rest singing through the seal.

He is the Sea Sovereign's chief tributary in the League, and his ships are how the [[Azure Wave Palace]] means to carry the dragon pearl home once someone steals it from the [[Floating Peak Continent]].
The bottom hull is a supply ship of the Scar's defenders, sunk in the Outer Demon War. Its hold is still sealed, and it still hums.
The white jiao wants a war to make his name. He pays poachers to raid his own nursery reefs so he can blame Jing fishermen.
He survives by selling the Beast Court the camps of rival raiders.
The Beast Court's Storm Roc lets the raiders operate. Nearly every cub they take comes from the White Ape King's lineages.
The last two winters came within days of a full bridge, and the tribes are choosing a Great Khan.
Outer demons climb it whenever the tide runs high. Most freeze on the upper steps. The ones that don't come ashore wearing whalers' faces.
The Hall's master has worked out that the outer arrays now carry load meant for the center. He told the Warden, and the Warden ordered him to tell no one else.
One sealed hall still answers to Upper Realm tokens, like parts of the [[Fallen Ladder]], and last winter it opened briefly for someone.
The patriarch pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]] for his escort routes, which is why his convoys never lose a hull to sea beasts.
The Heavenly Scale Pavilion buyers on the docks fix salvage prices together, and the Pavilion holds the notes on half the bead-makers in the Market of Water-Parting Beads.
Its elders have seen what climbs the [[Ice Stair]]. They chip the frozen ones out of the upper steps and sell them to the [[Eternal Night Palace]], which wants an outer demon's cultivation method.
The best forecaster in the harbor does not read the sky. She bribes an elder of the [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]], whose rods feel the drum in the eye before every lull.
The golems copy what visitors refine. The library has been learning the Sealed Era's alchemy for three thousand years, and some of its newer slips are better than anything outside.
The warm furnaces are still refining. They have tended the same batch since the Severance, and it is nearly done.
The bands are failing. Four have cracked since the tide turned, the last this decade, and the town council has agreed not to count them aloud.

The clerks enter one soul in twenty as lost to the sea and sell it to a broker who sets it into the cores of the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] puppets. This is why some of the Gate's puppets are not empty.
The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] court wants a sea war. War would let it conscript the coast's fishing families, who hide the last untested spirit-root children in the empire.
The claim maps are wrong on purpose. The Gate of Sinking and Rising's elders keep the richest valleys off them and drown anyone who finds one.
The buoys are the outermost ring of the seal array, not markers. For eleven years the northern bells have rung on still nights with nothing crossing, and always from the inside.

The eldest sage is brother to the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]]'s Old Tortoise. Through the two of them, the sea and the land beasts have been talking for a century, and the subject is humans.
The whale road is narrowing. Each year the pods swim closer to the coast, as if something were pushing them away from the Rim.
The temple tags ransomed whales with prayer beads and sells their tracks to a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] whaling consortium. Compassion here has a price list too.
The market is not empty. Its shopkeepers are still there, a half-step out of phase, and they remember every customer who did not pay.
The queens have married shark-folk for twelve generations. The royal children are half-bloods, and the sea spares the kingdom for their sake.
An Ascent Age master sleeps sealed in a cave abode on the crack's wall. His arrays are drawing qi from divers to wake him, and he is close. He sealed himself at Body Integration.
The arrays are built for a tribulation he cannot survive without the pearl. If age or war forces him to rise early, he dies, and the court splits between generals and sages.

Forged Watch tokens from [[Ten Thousand Sails]] circulate on the quay. The Merit Office lets them, because anyone desperate enough to buy a forgery is worth following, and some of them lead to the [[Void Choir]].
The fog thickens because the Sand Sea is spreading west, faster than anyone in Myriad Sands admits.
The prince quietly funds his raids. Every burned town drives the Ancestor Emperor's other heirs to beg that prince for protection.
The League's current speaker pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]], and the agenda of its next meeting was written in the Sea Sovereign's court.
Fewer than half the prisoners are Choir. The rest saw something on duty they were told never to speak of, and spoke.
The jiao's soul is still in the skull. It hears every oath and reports it to the Sea Sovereign, which is how he knows which League lords to buy.
The Sovereign has chosen theft over war. He is quietly shopping among human sects for thieves who can walk into the Floating Peaks.
Last spring two whalers who stayed the winter walked back into town. Their families took them home and have let no one see them since.
The [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] is its largest oil buyer, through a merchant front, and has privately asked it not to stop whaling.
The lulls are getting shorter and less regular, and the abbey has stopped publishing its count of them.
He feeds near the Ice Stair on purpose. Whatever climbs it, he eats, and he is the only reason the climbers are few.

The drum is the heart of a storm wall raised around the Scar in the First Sealing, and the belt is its last working arc. Each beat answers a pulse from the Scar, and the beats are coming closer together.
It drains toward the Nether Shard. Every Ghost Month a few thousand souls go down it, registered by neither court.
Not every rift opens onto empty void. Twice this century something has come through a large one, and the [[Seal Watch]] burned the nearby islands and called it a fire.
The frozen host faces south because it came from the north. It climbed the [[Ice Stair]] while the war raged at the Scar, and the stair is still a door.
The yards are laying a hundred hulls for a buyer paying through the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]]. It is the Great Jing's admiralty, and the fleet is meant for these isles.
It is an Ascent Age sea beast, one of those the tide is waking, and it rolled over in its sleep last spring.
He had stopped paying the [[Azure Wave Palace]]. His crews' souls serve in the Sovereign's court now, and the hands on the divers' ankles are theirs, begging to be taken up.
Their best ink is not theirs. It is milked from something much larger at the trench bottom, and keeping it calm is getting harder.
The herds are not wild. Something still whistles them home at dusk, and it has noticed the egg thieves.
Its forecasts come from an outer demon it keeps caged in nested space, which feels the void sea pressing on the world.
Each Kingdom of Calm Waves servant carries a sea-clan sigil under the tongue. Whoever buys one buys the Sovereign an ear.
Something on the far side holds the large rifts open a few breaths longer every year.
Every name carved so far was wrong. The right one would unpay the price of the seal, and the Pale Sovereign of the [[Court of No Light]] knows exactly what that would cost.
Its best puppet came up from the [[Black Throat Abyss]] holding something and has refused every command since. The master keeps it chained in his cellar and is afraid to unmake it.
The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has told the Sect of Gleaned Relics to find one sword above all others, and not to draw it if they do.
The old texts about Ascent Age masters walking out along the falling water describe this. The shard was a waystation, and its far side faces the void sea, not Severed Heaven.
Every lord here pays the Sea Sovereign, and turtle sages below steer the current that names the isles. A lord who stops paying finds out when the current turns.
The quartermaster sells patrol schedules to the raiders, and the admiral lets him. Every raid justifies a bigger fleet.
The registry keeps two ledgers. Every rich claim in the isles has been sold twice, and the registrars decide which sale is real by who pays last.
She pays the [[Seal Watch]] in information, reporting every ship that drifts toward the buoys, and in return no Watch elder has ever come to clean out the stacks.
The chief general keeps a spy among the vault guards on the Floating Peaks, and has not told the Sovereign.
Elders whose terms have ended are still on the walls. Their sects keep receiving letters in their handwriting, written by the Watch's scribes.
The master is a turtle sage of the [[Turtle Archive]] in human form, and the academy is how the Sovereign chooses which island lords to buy next.
Substitution frees no one. The drowned soul goes into a court's ledger either way. The founder knows; the queue is simply the most profitable lie on the sea.
It is the storm wall's intake. Everything it swallows is carried down to cool the drum, and the chamber around the drum is full of ships.
The two courts settled the dispute in secret centuries ago and split the souls between them. The arguing on the water is theater to keep human sects out of the trade.

It will touch the world barrier within a century, long before the Floating Peak Continent's peaks. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] keeps a hidden post on its underside to record exactly what happens when it does.
Jing registrars on the coast sell the raiders lists of villages with untested spirit-root children, and take a share of every sale.
Its anchor fees are paid in secret by the [[Armillary Pavilion]], which wants the shards held at fixed heights as relay posts for a new Ladder.
The shards that rise are the ones with intact Ascent Age halls. They are not drifting; something on the Mirror's side is pulling them home.
The Apricot Grove Valley uses the Hall's revived strains to breed the blights it seeds in rival gardens. The Hall's master knows and takes the money.
The [[Pavilion of the Rising Tide]] rigs the spring auctions. The crown is paid a fixed fee, and the best children never reach the block.
Its biggest buyer is the [[Apricot Grove Valley]], through three layers of middlemen. The white jiao at the [[White Scale Barrier]] knows, and is saving the name for when he needs a war.
They have waited sixty-six thousand years for the array to be repaired, and they still keep its keys. It once linked to the Heaven Ladder.
The admiral refuses to register with the Court of No Light. The moment the fleet is registered, its souls belong to the Pale Sovereign, and he promised them they would stay together.
The rods are draining the drum in the eye. The abbot knows the storm is part of a seal, and has decided the abbey's growth matters more.
The guild knows which stacks will fall next, and is waiting for the one above the queen's hall.
The pearl walls are a ledger. Each pearl was wept for a shark-folk killed by humans, and the generals mean to collect on all of them.
The seal is failing faster than the Seal Watch reports. It has doubled its garrison and stopped granting leave.
A few shards still hold descendants of Severance survivors, cut off for sixty-six thousand years.
A few of the floating shards are slowly rising toward the Mirror.
The seal is the Nameless Sealer. Her cultivation has held Heaven's Scar shut for 3,127 years, and the rising tide is pulling it open faster than she can mend it.
Armillary Pavilion survey teams have climbed it in secret. The top is not broken. It was cut clean.
Some of their best puppets are not empty. The Gate's master does not know. The fullest of them holds the soul of a Body Integration immortal from the Age of the Ascent, awake and patient.

The Heavenly Scale Pavilion holds the debts of four great powers. If it called them in at once, two would fall. Every karmic oath the Pavilion writes is sworn to the Founding Scale, a Body Integration merchant no living client has met. Two of its Scale-Keepers are at Void Refinement.
Some of its leaders are possessed by outer demons who slipped out during the war. They are patient.
Outer demons are the Void Sea's native life. They feed on worlds' qi and are drawn to anything that pierces a world barrier.

The tide will peak in about two thousand years. The same pull that floods the world with qi is stretching the seal over Heaven's Scar, and the Seal Watch knows it is failing faster than it admits. A handful of Tribulation Transcenders are alive. Most hide from their last tribulation or wait for the tide's peak to ascend; the Nameless Sealer is bound inside the seal.

Apricot Grove Valley keeps its grip on the herb trade by quietly seeding blight in rival gardens. The Valley Master calls it hygiene. The Valley Master is a Void Refinement alchemist who has outlived three dynasties by keeping all of them in his debt.
On still nights the bones shift a little toward Ancestor Mountain. The Bone Ancestor is drawing what is left of his descendants back to him.
Sea-Crossing Temple has quietly bought the loan. If the kingdom defaults, the monks own the walls.
The camp's master is training a hundred outsiders, not tribesmen, as the Snow Wolf claimant's personal guard. He thinks a khan's guard should owe nothing to any tribe.
The Bear King knows what is taking the hunters, because it has taken bears too. He is afraid of it, and he has never been afraid of anything.
The last Great Khan died on the sea ice because an Ice-Fisher guide led his army onto a current lead. The tribe has never admitted it, and the Snow Wolf chief has started asking.
Time runs slower inside. The few who have been shut in through a closing came out seven years later having lived a single day.
The Mu salvage decree is a forgery. The Palace knows, and lets it stand because the Mu send their best finds to the Night Sovereign every year.
The lord died on the ice. The outer demon that escaped the Palace wears him now, feeds on travelers who steer for the lamp and keeps its own villagers fat and warm. The song is the Frozen Host's.
At the center, behind the last ward, an Ascent Age master sits frozen in meditation. He chose to sleep through the Ebb, and the rising tide is thawing him.
The lottery is rigged, and the Lan heir hates it. He has been smuggling hidden children south to the [[Sea-Crossing Temple]], and the Palace will notice the missing count by spring.
Its boss failed the Palace's Ash Gate thirty years ago and swore to bury a Palace elder in the ice before he dies. He has finally found a client who will pay for it.
Some of the black glass is not dead. It warms in the hand when someone nearby hums.
Their queen has sent an envoy to the Cold Jiao Mansion offering to guide its hunters into the Whale Tooth fjord.

The temple has been buying the coastal kingdoms' debts through the Heavenly Scale Pavilion brokers for fifty years. Within a generation it will own the Sand-Gazing Shore without converting a single king.
The king is not dying of age. The elder son's Palace patron has been salting his bread with Blood Salt Lake salt, a pinch a day.

The kingdom did not freeze by accident. Its king bargained with an outer demon for a cultivation method and paid with his people's warmth. His court has forgotten the bargain, and the Night Sovereign's envoys have started asking the ghost king to remember it.
The vanished elders were sent to the thaw works under the glacier. The Night Sovereign lets nobody who has seen a thawed demon come home.
The town is still inhabited. Its people descend from Severance survivors, speak an Ascent Age dialect and kill outsiders on sight, because the last visitors took their children.
The Palace wants those vents to pipe fire under the glacier for its thaw works. A third refusal will be answered with an army, and the old mother knows it.
The aurora is the world barrier glowing where it is thinnest, close to the Rim. It has doubled in brightness in a century as the tide stretches the barrier, and the steles have started to answer it.
It is where the escaped demon first fed. It eats voices first, so its prey cannot call for help, and it can speak in every voice it has eaten.
The shard is a piece of the central continent's old foundries, thrown out in the Severance. Somewhere inside is a forge that still remembers how the Ladder's jade was made.
The bodies are the Cornerstone Gang's work, paid for by whoever wants someone gone. The council knows, because two of its members are clients.
Some of the children taken north are grandparents in the Snow Wolf tribe now. The ghosts know their own blood when they see it, and do not touch it.
The clan wants the tableland's Ascent Age mammoth-king cores to refresh its thinning bloodline, and is buying the Fief of Ancient Tusks' debts to get them. The road is for the Pine's heartwood.
The Lord failed a dragon tribulation two centuries ago and is hoarding cold for a second try. He covets the glacier more than any toll.
The line is a formation. An Ascent Age alchemist built the lake as a cauldron, and the lid is still down there.
Outer demons climb the Rim here. The Frozen Host's scouts came up this way during the war, and the beacon flickers whenever something is climbing now.

The ice spreads further each winter because the glacier's cold is spreading. Within thirty years the Fair will stand on ocean ice half the year, and the Snow Wolves will be able to reach it in a night's ride.
She is losing. Two of her own sub-chiefs have taken Snow Wolf gold, and the Old Mammoth clan has stopped sending calves to her herds.
The glacier began creeping faster forty years ago, the year the first thawed demon escaped. The Watch's geomancers have measured it, and the Warden has sealed their report.
The master has worked out why the aurora is brightening and sent her figures to the Armillary Pavilion. The reply asked her, politely, to stop publishing.

The Palace is drawing the northern springs' fire through lava tubes to heat its thaw works under the glacier. When those springs die the north basin freezes, and the Musk Ox Tribe will blame the farmers.
The second patrol found one survivor. He hummed all the way back to the fortress and was quietly killed there, and the Watch has told no one.
The Spine is warming with the tide. Three volcanoes dead since the Dim Age began smoking this decade, and one of them is the mountain the Palace is built on.
The backward shadow is cast by the Mirror. The stone is counting down the years to the tide's peak, and its count agrees with the Armillary Pavilion's own tables.
The caves are the Palace's thaw works. Its tunnels reach the Frozen Host from below, and the demon that escaped forty years ago walked out through them.
The ship came down the Ladder. Its hold is sealed, and the harbor master's family has kept the key for a thousand years without knowing what it is.
Two of their shamans have started humming the same tune in their sleep, and their children have picked it up without being taught.
The treatise was carved by the sect that built the Slumbering City, and its last chapter is not about ice. It is about sealing outer demons, and whoever froze the Frozen Host had read it.
